chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Abī Ayyūb, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
"Whoever confesses against himself to a hadd punishment, I would carry it out upon him, except rajm; for if he confesses against himself and then denies it, he is not to be stoned."

key_terms.أَقَرَّ: confessed or acknowledged legally against oneself
key_terms.أَقَمْتُهُ: I would establish or enforce it
key_terms.بِحَدٍّ: to a hadd punishment, meaning a fixed penal offense under sacred law
key_terms.جَحَدَ: denied or retracted after prior acknowledgment
key_terms.لَمْ يُرْجَمْ: he is not to be stoned
key_terms.نَفْسِهِ: his own person or self, indicating self-incrimination

ai.seo_question: What happens if someone confesses to a hadd offense and then retracts the confession in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding judicial confession to a hadd offense. It establishes that hadd punishments may be enforced on the basis of self-confession, except in the case of rajm, where a later retraction prevents the stoning penalty from being carried out.
